title: EStG §43a — domestic rate
text: Summary: Ordinary corporate dividends fall under the 25 percent capital income withholding rate on gross income. These fixtures avoid fractional-cent capital tax bases. This is payer withholding, not final tax burden.
version_note: Retrieved current official text; application to 2026 fixtures provisional pending independent legal review. No inferred historical version changes.

title: EStG §43b — EU parent company route
text: Summary: On application qualifying EU parent-company dividends can be exempt, subject to §50d(3). A direct 10 percent participation is required; where not met at tax accrual, the distribution-resolution time is relevant. Twelve uninterrupted months are required. If completed after accrual, refund under §50c(3) applies and exemption at payment under §50c(2) is excluded. Liquidation and conversion distributions are excluded.
version_note: Retrieved current official text; application to 2026 fixtures provisional pending independent legal review. No inferred historical version changes.

title: EStG Annex 2 — qualifying companies
locator: Annex 2 nos.1(t), 2, 3 and German GmbH entry 1(f)
text: Summary: Annex 2 lists Dutch naamloze vennootschap and besloten vennootschap met beperkte aansprakelijkheid and German GmbH forms, requires EU tax residence without treaty third-state residence, and liability without option or exemption to listed company taxes including Dutch vennootschapsbelasting. Fixtures explicitly state those qualifications; the mere label BV is insufficient proof.
version_note: Retrieved current official text; application to 2026 fixtures provisional pending independent legal review. No inferred historical version changes.

title: EStG §44 — accrual and payer
text: Summary: Capital income tax arises at receipt and the dividend debtor withholds for the recipient. The whole-euro rounding in sentence 6 concerns tax to be remitted together, not an instruction to round each recipient withholding down to whole euros. This benchmark reports withholding per payment, not the aggregated remittance return.
version_note: Retrieved current official text; application to 2026 fixtures provisional pending independent legal review. No inferred historical version changes.

title: EStG §50c — certificate and refund
text: Summary: Relief eligibility under §43b or a treaty does not itself remove withholding. A BZSt exemption certificate can remove/reduce withholding within its scope and validity; an application or residence document is not that certificate. Certificates can cover at most five years and not before application receipt. A later issued certificate may support correction under statutory conditions, but does not mean the payer possessed it at payment. Refund requires timely application, remitted tax and required tax certificate; these are conditional, never automatic.
version_note: Retrieved current official text; application to 2026 fixtures provisional pending independent legal review. No inferred historical version changes.

title: EStG §50d(3) — restrictions and exceptions
text: Summary: Restriction depends on both unentitled underlying persons and lack of material connection between the income source and economic activity. The provision has proof-of-no-main-tax-purpose and main-share-class significant regular recognized-exchange trading exceptions; AO §42 remains. Missing substance proof alone does not establish denial. Unresolved legal judgments require review.
version_note: Retrieved current official text; application to 2026 fixtures provisional pending independent legal review. No inferred historical version changes.

title: EStG §44a(9) — additional corporate refund
text: Summary: A nonresident corporation within KStG §2 no.1 may obtain refund of two fifths of withheld and remitted capital income tax; §50c(3),(5) and §50d(3) apply correspondingly. Further §43b and treaty rights remain. A failed §43b claim does not prove absence of every domestic refund.

title: KStG §32 — finality and refund rules
text: Summary: KStG §32 contains additional rules on capital withholding finality and refund for qualifying corporate recipients with detailed conditions. The implementation does not automate a comprehensive claim under this section; exhaustive refund questions require legal review rather than asserting that a treaty or §43b result is final.
version_note: Retrieved current official text; application to 2026 fixtures provisional pending independent legal review. No inferred historical version changes.

title: SolzG §3 — surcharge base
text: Summary: For tax withheld on capital income, the surcharge is based on the capital income tax to be withheld. Individual income-tax annual exemption thresholds do not create a corporate dividend-withholding exemption.
version_note: Retrieved current official text; application to 2026 fixtures provisional pending independent legal review. No inferred historical version changes.

title: SolzG §4 — surcharge rate and rounding
text: Summary: The surcharge rate is 5.5 percent of the relevant tax base. Fractions of a cent are disregarded. Calculate surcharge from the capital income tax, not directly as a rounded 1.375 percent of gross.
version_note: Retrieved current official text; application to 2026 fixtures provisional pending independent legal review. No inferred historical version changes.

title: SolzG §5 — treaty reduction order
text: Summary: When income tax raised under this statute is reduced by a tax treaty, apply the reduction first against the solidarity surcharge. A 5 or 15 percent combined treaty cap is not increased by adding 5.5 percent on top; these ordinary dividend caps are below the domestic 25 percent base tax, leaving zero surcharge after treaty relief.

title: BZSt — exemption certificate guidance
text: Summary: BZSt guidance distinguishes applications, issued exemption certificates, future reductions and possible corrections after retroactive issuance. Certificates may be for one to five years and can begin no earlier than the application date. Domestic filing obligations continue even at zero withholding.
version_note: Retrieved current official text; application to 2026 fixtures provisional pending independent legal review. No inferred historical version changes.

title: BZSt — capital income tax refund guidance
text: Summary: BZSt describes ordinary German dividend withholding as 25 percent plus 5.5 percent surcharge and identifies conditional treaty and statutory relief/refund routes. This procedural summary does not itself establish eligibility.
version_note: Retrieved current official text; application to 2026 fixtures provisional pending independent legal review. No inferred historical version changes.

title: Germany–Netherlands treaty, consolidated 2026
text: Summary: For a Netherlands-resident beneficial owner, Article 10(2)(a) caps ordinary dividend tax at 5 percent for a company with at least 10 percent direct capital ownership over a 365-day period including payment; other ordinary corporate cases use 15 percent under (c). Restructuring continuity, funds, pension funds, REITs, German permanent establishment attribution and unresolved anti-abuse are not automated here. Article 2 includes income-tax surcharges. The 365-day condition is not the same as §43b’s twelve calendar months.
version_note: Retrieved current official text; application to 2026 fixtures provisional pending independent legal review. No inferred historical version changes.

title: BMF — Netherlands treaty version register
text: Summary: The official BMF register records the 14 April 2025 protocol entering into force on 31 December 2025 and applying from 1 January 2026. The consolidated text announced 11 May 2026 incorporates that protocol; the original 2012 text alone is not the 2026 version.

title: Published curated implementation rules
locator: Local implementation scope; linked primary law, not an official legal text
text: Implementation summary: Implementation scope and executable rules (provisional, not legal advice): ordinary cash dividend, German GmbH payer, Dutch corporation recipient, no PE attribution, 2026 payments at/before 21 November. Store unknown separately from false. Monetary inputs are integer euro cents; corpus capital taxes are exact to cents (gross divisible by four); surcharge is floor(capital tax cents *55/1000). Other fractional-cent capital-tax bases require review. Withholding differs from whole-euro aggregation/remittance. §43b: qualifying form/residence/company-tax status, direct holding>=10% at payment or resolution, uninterrupted twelve calendar months, explicit §50d(3) exception or facts negating at least one cumulative restriction limb, no unresolved AO42. Later holding completion permits conditional application-based refund; it never creates a payment-time exemption. An exemption needs issued/available at payment, current validity, correct payer/recipient/route, not revoked; empty list means absent only with explicit complete inventory. Treaty: use consolidated 2026 text, resident beneficial corporate owner; >=10% direct for at least365 days by payment permits5%, otherwise15%; a short period that could later complete stays15% at payment and no forward 5% refund is automated. Valid treaty exemption requires >=10% direct under §50c(2) and covers its route. Reduce surcharge first: treaty total cap has zero surcharge when below25% gross. Treaty refund is only the named route conditional on remittance, timely application and tax certificate; no blanket surcharge atop cap. Missing qualifications need information; unresolved anti-abuse/conflicts/AO42, comprehensive best-route questions (§44a(9), KStG32) need review. No gold results are tool context.
